A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLB research, with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original contamination measurements, LVLM evaluation results, sensitivity analyses, and human verification of 2,100 transformed samples.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds uncertainty estimates, editor and judge ablations, further contamination analyses, and image-captioning experiments.

M1.justification: The main VQA bootstrapping strategies and judge loop remain unchanged. Appendix A.13 introduces a captioning adaptation that generates new GPT-4V reference captions after editing images, whereas the original VQA procedure preserves the existing answer.

E1.justification: Appendix A.13 adds image captioning, extending actual evaluation beyond VQA. COCO-Caption, previously used as a contamination reference corpus, becomes an evaluation benchmark. The five original VQA benchmarks remain covered.

E2.justification: Appendix A.8/Table 9 adds component-level comparisons against PowerPaint: BrushNet for object insertion and Stable Diffusion for outpainting. The LVLM membership in the retained main comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include controlled editor substitutions, human verification of samples without judge filtering, and captioning evaluation on 500 randomly sampled COCO-Caption pairs with newly generated references. Existing VQA subsets, temperature, and principal settings remain unchanged. Table 15 does not specify the captioning scoring metric.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's outpainting sensitivity and post-judge verification, v3 adds editor and judge ablations (A.8–A.9), analyses relating accuracy changes to image similarity and question length (A.10), separate linguistic-strategy contamination analyses (A.12), and additional error and generation-failure cases (Figures 14–15). These substantially expand validation of the framework.

E5.justification: V1 provides no seed counts or uncertainty estimates. Appendix A.7.2 newly describes results as averages over five randomly seeded dataset variants and reports standard deviations for seven strategies across three datasets and three LVLMs in Table 8. This establishes systematic uncertainty reporting, but does not establish an increase in the underlying run count.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New tables report editor comparisons, pre-judge verification rates, rejection iterations, diagnostic relationships, linguistic contamination rates, and captioning scores. For example, Table 9 reports TransCore-M SEEDBench V1 accuracy of 69.10 with PowerPaint and 70.91 with BrushNet; these are newly compared configurations, not a revision of the original method's performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of static and dynamic samples, transformations, and strategy composition remain unchanged. The added appendices contain empirical analyses and conceptual explanations, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: VLB enables dynamic multimodal evaluation with flexible complexity, reduced contamination, and exposure of LVLM limitations. The new experiments support the existing generality claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning reliability across random variants, interchangeable image editors, and applicability to captioning. The original visual-attention and linguistic explanations largely remain. Appendix A.12 additionally interprets reduced contamination as generated questions being absent from pretraining, although Table 14 still reports nonzero contamination rates.

D1.justification: Table 7 newly lists model parameter sizes, and A.5 documents independent human judgments, majority voting, and rejection of ties. A.13 supplies the caption-generation procedure. The code pointer changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: Related work adds Shah et al. (2019), Gokhale et al. (2020), and Selvaraju et al. (2020), distinguishing their VQA reformulations from VLB's automatic applicability. It also clarifies the contrast with Chen et al. (2024a). New appendix citations cover alternative editors and contextual background, while the central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained. Changes include localized wording and cross-reference corrections, updated author and publication information, acknowledgments, additional appendix subsections, and an expanded explanation of user interaction in A.11. There is no extensive rewriting of the existing paper.

P2.justification: V3 substantially extends the displayed evidence through Tables 7–15 and new error/failure Figures 14–15. Figure 3 gains explanatory labels and corrects L3 from irrelevant to relevant context; Figures 8–9 receive more precise captions. Existing figures and tables are largely retained, with some relocation and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: V1 showed consistency after judging but did not isolate the judge's contribution or report variation across generated datasets. V3's unfiltered-sample control, alternative-editor ablations, and five-seed standard deviations address important validation gaps in the central framework. Added implementation disclosures also improve reproducibility. The unspecified captioning metric and A.12's overstatement of nonzero contamination reductions weaken some additions, but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in core validation.
